Rashi on Ketubot 21b:10:1.hebrew: וקרא ערער על הא' - שהוא פסול:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:10:1.english: And [someone] raised a challenge against one [of them] - [Claiming] that he is disqualified.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:10:2.english: Before they signed - The two [other] judges on the ratification.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:10:3.english: They testify - About this [judge] that he is fit.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:10:4.english: Once they signed - They become interested parties in the testimony, for [it is] a disgrace to them that they sat with an unfit [person] in judgment.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:1:1.hebrew: איקלע רבנאי למיזבן שומשמי - גרסי', ולא גרסי' "דאיקלע", ולא גרסינן "לגבן". ולאו רמי אמרה, דא"א לומר כן, שאמר רמי עדות זו על אמימר ורב אשי, שהרי רב אשי כמה דורות היה אחריו, דאמרינן בקדושין (דף עב.): "יום שמת רב יהודה נולד רבא, יום שמת רבא נולד רב אשי":
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:1:1.english: Ravnai happened [to come] to buy sesame - [This is what] we read, and we do not read "that [he] happened [to come]" [de'ikla], nor do we read "to us" [legabban]. And Rami [bar Yehezkel] did not say it, for it is impossible to say so — that Rami gave this testimony regarding Ameimar and Rav Ashi — since Rav Ashi was several generations after him, as we say in Kiddushin (72a): "On the day that Rav Yehudah died, Rava was born; on the day that Rava died, Rav Ashi was born."

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:1:2.english: The father of your mother - Rami bar Hama.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:1.english: Three [judges] who sat - In a court.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:2.hebrew: לקיים השטר - ובלא העדאת עדים שיעידו על כתב ידן, לפי שהדיינין עצמן מכירין אותה. השנים מכירין אותה ואחד אינו מכיר:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:2.english: To ratify the document - And [this is] without having witnesses testify about their handwriting, because the judges themselves recognize it. The two recognize it and one does not recognize [it].

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:3.english: Before they signed - [That is,] the two [judges] on the ratification [document].

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:4.english: They testify - before the third [judge] that this is the handwriting of the signatories.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:5.hebrew: וחותם - עמהם על מה שכותבין, "אשרנוהי וקיימנוהי לשטרא דנן במותב תלתא, דאשתמודענא דחתימת ידא דסהדי היא":
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:5.english: And he signs - with them on what they write: "We have confirmed and ratified this document in a session of three, as we have recognized that it is the signature of the witnesses."

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:6.hebrew: משחתמו אין מעידין - דחתימה קמייתא בשקרא הוה, דלאו תלתא הוו דידעי:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:2:6.english: Once they signed, they may not testify - For the first signature was false, since they were not three who knew [the signatures].

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:1.hebrew: ומי כתבינן - לאשרתא דידיה, בתמיה. וכי קודם שנתקיים לפני שלשתן יכתבו "במותב תלתא הוינא ואשתמודענא כו'":
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:1.english: And do we write - [i.e.,] his ratification, [asked] in astonishment: Before [the document] was authenticated before the three of them, would they write, "We were in a session of three and recognized [the signatures], etc."?

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:2.hebrew: אשרתא - לשון חוזק, שמחזקים [את השטר] וכותבין אשרנוהי:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:2.english: Asharta [ratification] - An expression of strengthening, for they strengthen [the document] and write, "We have ratified it."

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:3.hebrew: דנכתבא מקמי דניחוו סהדי כו' - עד שלא העידו העדים על כתב ידם, כתבו הדיינין: "במותב תלתא הוינא, ונפיק שטרא דנן קדמנא, ואסהידו פלוני ופלוני אחתימת ידייהו, ואשרנוהי וקיימנוהי":
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:3:3.english: That was written before the witnesses testified, etc. - Before the witnesses testified regarding their handwriting, the judges wrote: "We were in a session of three [judges], and this document was produced before us, and so-and-so and so-and-so testified regarding their signatures, and we ratified it and confirmed it."

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:5:1.english: A witness becomes a judge - For the two [judges] testified regarding the signatures.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:5:2.hebrew: צריכין להעיד בפני כל אחד ואחד - שאם העידו בפני השנים, אין הג' יכול לחתום, דהא הכא הוצרכו השנים להעיד בפני הג':
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:5:2.english: They must testify before each and every one - For if [witnesses] testified before the two [judges], the third [judge] cannot sign, since here the two had to testify before the third.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:6:1.hebrew: דלמא לעולם צריכין - להעיד, שאין עדות אלא ע"י הגדת עדות:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:6:1.english: Perhaps [they] actually require - [witnesses] to testify, for there is no testimony except through a statement of testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:6:2.english: And here it is different, as the statement [of testimony] is fulfilled - Before the single [judge] who does not recognize [the signatures].

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:7:1.english: As [the] statement [of testimony] is not fulfilled at all - If they did not testify before him.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:1.english: Three saw it - [This] refers to the testimony of the new moon.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:2.english: And they [constitute] a court - [They are] of the Sanhedrin who sanctify the month.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:3.hebrew: יעמדו השנים - להיות עדים. והתם פרכינן: לא תהא שמיעה גדולה מראיה? ומוקמינן לה כשראוהו בלילה, לפיכך אם לא יעידו לבקר, על מה יאמרו מקודש:
Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:3.english: The two should stand - To be witnesses. And there [in Rosh HaShana] we ask: Should hearing [testimony] be greater than seeing [the moon themselves]? And we establish it [as referring to a case] where they saw it at night; therefore, if they do not testify in the morning, on what [basis] would they say, "Sanctified"?

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:4.english: As an individual is not deemed credible - To sanctify the month alone.

Rashi on Ketubot 21b:8:5.english: Let them sit in their place - after they have testified before him [the individual judge].

Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:3:1.hebrew: האמר רב פפי האי אשרתא - תימה דפריך מדרב פפי, ובפרק הכותב (לקמן כתובות דף פה. ושם) מסיק דליתא לדרב פפי מדרב נחמן כו', ועוד דבפ' כל הגט (גיטין כו: ושם) מסיק דרב לית ליה דרב פפי, והיכי פריך הכא מדרב פפי אמילתיה דרב? מיהו הא איכא לתרץ, דאלישנא דאמרי לה משמיה דרב הונא פריך. ואין לומר דהכי פריך: כיון דאמר משחתמו אין מעידין לפניו וחותם, אלמא חיישינן למיחזי כשקרא, אם כן משכתבו עד שלא חתמו נמי, דכתיבה נמי מיחזי כשקרא; דא"כ הוה קשיא דרב אדרב, דהכא חייש למיחזי כשקרא, ובפרק כל הגט (שם) לא חייש, אלא טעמא דמשחתמו דמי לנוגעים בעדות, כעין שפירש בקונט' גבי ההוא שקרא ערער על אחד מהן. ותירץ ר"ת, דדרך הש"ס להקשות אפילו מדבר דלא הוי הלכתא הכי. ופוסק ר"ת דכתבינן אורכתא אפילו אמטלטלי דכפריה, דלא קיי"ל כרב פפי דחייש למיחזי כשקרא, אע"ג דפריך מינה; ופריך נמי מנהרדעי בכמה מקומות בפרק שבועת העדות (שבועות דף לג: ושם) ובפרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מט.): "והאמרי נהרדעי לא כתבינן אורכתא" כו'. וי"מ: "וליתא" דקאמר בהכותב ובפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף כו: ושם), דלא בעי למימר דליתא לדרב פפי, אלא דליתא לקושיא, שאין לדמות אשרתא שהוא מעשה ב"ד לשאר שטרות, דבמעשה ב"ד לכ"ע חיישינן למיחזי כשקרא. ור"י מדנפי"ר תירץ, דלכתחלה ודאי חיישינן למיחזי כשקרא, כדאמר להו רב לספרי: "כי יתביתו בהיני" כו' (ב"ב דף קעב.), אבל בדיעבד לא חיישינן; ולהכי פריך הכא, דהוי לכתחלה. והא דקאמר דליתא לדרב פפי, היינו דיעבד, דההיא איתתא דהכותב (לקמן כתובות דף פה. ושם), כיון שהיתה צריכה לחזור לב"ד, כדיעבד דמי. והרשאה נמי דכתבינן אמטלטלי דכפריה, היינו משום כיון דאינו יכול לילך שם, כדיעבד דמי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:3:1.english: Didn't Rav Pappi say... This ratification [of judges] - It is astonishing that [the Gemara] raises an objection from [the statement of] Rav Pappi, whereas in the chapter [entitled] Hakotev (below, Ketubot 85a, and there [in the parallel]), [the Gemara] concludes that [the ruling of] Rav Pappi is not accepted, [refuted] from [the statement of] Rav Nachman, etc. And furthermore, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 26b, and there), [the Gemara] concludes that Rav does not hold [the view] of Rav Pappi, so how can [the Gemara] raise an objection here from Rav Pappi against the statement of Rav? However, this [latter difficulty] can be resolved, [by saying] that [the Gemara] is raising the objection against the version that states it in the name of Rav Huna. And one cannot say that this is what [the Gemara] is asking: "Since he said that once they have signed, they may not testify before him and have him sign [the ratification], evidently we are concerned for [what] appears like a lie; if so, [the same should apply] from when they wrote [the ratification] before they signed as well, for the writing also appears like a lie"; for if so, Rav would contradict Rav — since here he is concerned for [what] appears like a lie, whereas in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (there) he is not concerned [for it], rather the reason [for invalidating] once they have signed is that they are like interested parties in the testimony, similar to what Rashi explained regarding one who raised a challenge against one of them. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that it is the way of the Talmud to raise an objection even from something where the halakhah is not like that. And Rabbeinu Tam rules that we write a power of attorney even for movable property that [the defendant] denied [having], for we do not establish [the halakhah] like Rav Pappi, who is concerned for [what] appears like a lie, even though [the Gemara] raises an objection from it; and [similarly, the Gemara] also raises an objection from the Nehardeans in several places — in the chapter [entitled] Shevuat HaEdut (Shevuot 33b, and there) and in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a): "But didn't the Nehardeans say we do not write a power of attorney," etc. [even though the halakhah does not follow them]. And some explain: [the expression] "and it is not [so]" that [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] Hakotev and in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 26b, and there) does not mean to say that [the ruling of] Rav Pappi is not accepted, rather that the objection is not valid, for one cannot compare a ratification [of judges], which is a court act, to other documents, because in a court act, according to all opinions, we are concerned for [what] appears like a lie. And Rabbi Yitzchak of Dampierre answered that ab initio (lekhatchilah) we are certainly concerned for [what] appears like a lie, as Rav said to his scribes: "When you sit in Hini," etc. (Bava Batra 172a), but ex post facto (bedi'avad) we are not concerned; and therefore [the Gemara] raises an objection here, because it is ab initio. And that which [the Gemara] says that [the ruling of] Rav Pappi is not accepted refers to an ex post facto situation, for that woman in [the chapter] Hakotev (below, Ketubot 85a, and there), since she would have needed to return to the court, is considered like ex post facto. And [the reason] we also write a power of attorney for movable property that [the defendant] denied is because, since [the claimant] cannot go there [himself], it is considered like ex post facto.

Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:5:1.hebrew: וש"מ דיינין המכירין חתימת עדים א"צ להעיד בפניהם - דקס"ד דצריך להעיד בפניהם, אע"ג דלא תהא שמיעה גדולה מראייה, לפי שהיו נראין יותר בית דין; דכשאין מעידין בפניהם, אין נראה אלא כעד מפי עד. ומטעם זה הצריכו ג' בקיום שטרות, דהוה סגי בב', אלא משום דבעינן שיהא ב"ד, כדפרישית. ועוד אומר ר"י דס"ד דצרי' להעיד בפניהם, משום דפעמים אין מכירין אלא על ידי שראו בלילה, דליכא למימר לא תהא שמיעה גדולה מראייה, דשמיעה אינה יכולה להיות בלילה, כדאמר בר"ה (דף כה: ושם) דחקירת עדים כתחלת דין דמי, ותחלת דין אינו אלא ביום כדאמרינן בסנהדרין (דף לב.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:5:1.english: And conclude from it [that] judges who recognize the signatures of witnesses do not need [other witnesses] to testify before them - For it might have entered one's mind that [witnesses] need to testify before them — even though hearing [testimony] should not be greater than seeing [the signatures oneself] — because they would appear more like a court; for when [witnesses] do not testify before them, it only looks like hearsay [lit. a witness from the mouth of a witness]. And for this reason they required three [judges] for the ratification of documents, for two would have sufficed, except that we require that it be a court, as I explained [above]. And furthermore, R. Yitzchak says that it might have entered one's mind that [witnesses] need to testify before them because sometimes they only recognize [the signatures] by having seen [them] at night, in which case one cannot say "hearing should not be greater than seeing," since hearing [testimony] cannot take place at night — as it says in Rosh Hashanah (25b, and ad loc.) that the examination of witnesses is like the beginning of a judgment, and the beginning of a judgment is only during the day, as we say in Sanhedrin (32a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:5:2.hebrew: בפני כל אחד ואחד - דס"ד כיון שהעידו בפני שנים, יכול השלישי לכתוב על סמך השנים, אע"פ שלא העידו בפניו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:5:2.english: Before each and every one - For you might have thought [that] since they testified before two [judges], the third [judge] can write [the ratification] relying on the two, even though they did not testify before him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:9:1.hebrew: הנח לעדות החדש דאורייתא - ובדאורייתא אין עד נעשה דיין. וטעמא דאין עד נעשה דיין, משום דבעינן שיעידו לפני הדיינין, כמו שמפרש רשב"ם, דכתיב: "ועמדו שני האנשים" — אלו העדים, "לפני ה'" — אלו הדיינין. וי"מ: משום דבעינן עדות שאתה יכול להזימה, ואם העדים נעשו דיינין — עדות שאין אתה יכול להזימה היא, שלא יקבלו הזמה על עצמן. ומיהו לפי טעם זה, אם העדים קרובים לדיינין — אינם יכולים להעיד, דלא יקבלו הזמה עליהם? אלא כיון דבני הזמה נינהו בב"ד אחר, "עדות שאתה יכול להזימה" קרינא בהו — ה"נ יהיה הדיין נעשה עד. ודוקא בעד המעיד אמרינן דאין עד נעשה דיין, דשייכי הני טעמי; אבל עד שאינו צריך להעיד — כגון שיש אחרים שיעידו, או כגון שראוהו ביום, שאינו צריך להעיד, דלא תהא שמיעה גדולה מראייה — נעשה דיין. ודווקא בדיני ממונות; אבל בדיני נפשות, אפילו עד שאין צריך להעיד אין נעשה דיין, לר"ע דאמר במסכת מכות (דף ו. ושם): "אפילו הן מאה — כולן עדים". וטעמא מפרש בפרק ראוהו ב"ד (ר"ה דף כו. ושם): משום דכתיב "והצילו העדה", והנך כיון דחזו דקטל — תו לא חזי ליה זכותא. ודווקא בדאורייתא, אבל בדרבנן, אפילו עד המעיד נעשה דיין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 21b:9:1.english: "Leave [the case of] testimony [to sanctify] the month, as [it is mandated] by Torah [law]" - And in [cases of] Torah law, a witness cannot become a judge. And the reason that a witness cannot become a judge is because we require that they testify before the judges, as Rashbam explains, for it is written: "Then the two men shall stand" — these are the witnesses — "before the Lord" — these are the judges. And some explain: because we require testimony that you are able to refute through hazamah [collusive-witness rebuttal], and if the witnesses become judges, it is testimony that you cannot refute through hazamah, since they will not accept hazamah against themselves. However, according to this reason, if the witnesses are related to the judges, are they unable to testify because [the judges] will not accept hazamah against them? Rather, since they are subject to hazamah in another court, we apply to them [the requirement of] "testimony that you are able to refute through hazamah" — here too, let the judge become a witness. And specifically with regard to a witness who testifies do we say that a witness cannot become a judge, because these reasons apply; however, a witness who does not need to testify — such as where there are others who will testify, or where they saw [the event] during the day, so that he does not need to testify, for hearing [testimony] should not be greater than seeing [it oneself] — he may become a judge. And [this applies] specifically in monetary cases; however, in capital cases, even a witness who does not need to testify cannot become a judge, according to Rabbi Akiva, who says in Tractate Makkot (6a, and there [in the Gemara]): "Even if there are a hundred [who saw it], all of them are witnesses." And the reason is explained in the chapter [entitled] Ra'uhu Beit Din (Rosh Hashanah 26a, and there): because it is written, "And the congregation shall deliver [the slayer]," and these [witnesses], since they saw him kill, will no longer see any merit for him [to acquit him]. And [all of this applies] specifically in [cases of] Torah law, whereas in rabbinic [cases], even a witness who testifies may become a judge.
